comparator.name: Bachelor Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: TU/e's current official programme, Education Guide and 2026-2027 Bachelor AUBS Course Guide, checked 2026-10-03, describe a three-year, 180-EC bachelor for students starting in 2023-2024 and after. The formal structure is 130 EC of core study, 40 EC of electives and 10 EC of Impact of Technology study. The common first year combines calculus and built-environment theory with four successive projects and orientation across Architectural Urban Design and Engineering, Building Physics and Services, Structural Engineering and Design, and Urban Systems and Real Estate. Students then select one track, take its core courses and projects, complete a multidisciplinary project and finish with a 10-EC Bachelor End Project. The complete 130/40/10 allocation is retained below because the official guide defines the variable track and elective curriculum rather than one universal course list.
components: AUBS core programme, selected track, projects and Bachelor End Project

Compulsory built-environment formation includes the common first-year courses and projects, one of four later tracks, quantitative and design-oriented research methods, a multidisciplinary project and a 10-EC Bachelor End Project.
Genuine elective space used to deepen the selected track, combine tracks or build a thematic profile; at least 30 EC must be level two or three and at least 5 EC level three.
The university-wide engineering-and-society line consists of two ITEC courses.

exception.reason: TU/e's AUBS bachelor is a project- and studio-intensive built-environment engineering degree. Its common first year integrates calculus, architecture and the city, urban systems, healthy and sustainable environments, structural statics, circularity and energy performance, and structure and architecture with four successive design or research projects. The later programme requires one of four coherent tracks and its project sequence: architectural and urban design, building physics and services, structural engineering and design, or urban systems and real estate. All routes culminate in multidisciplinary project work and a discipline-specific Bachelor End Project. UCR offers useful adjacent courses in spatial planning, GIS and earth observation, sustainable energy and life-cycle analysis, nature-based design, product design, heritage and quantitative methods. It has no architecture or urban-design studio sequence, building-physics and building-services sequence, structural statics and materials progression, construction-technology education, architectural drawing and modelmaking formation, or built-environment engineering capstone. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore replace the target's defining studio, technical and project spine with adjacent liberal-arts and sustainability study and would not be an academically defensible comparison.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-2027 AUBS guide and current Education Guide account for all 180 EC as 130 EC core, 40 EC electives and 10 EC ITEC. Year one is common and explicitly orients students across AUDE, BPS, SED and USRE through built-environment courses and four projects. In years two and three, students choose one track, complete its core courses and projects, and use genuine elective space for depth, cross-track study or a thematic profile. The current guide requires a multidisciplinary project before the 10-EC Bachelor End Project. Illustrative named course and project lists include Histories of Architecture and Urbanism, Architecture and Technology, Dimensioning of Structures, Urban Planning, Building Services, Concrete and Masonry Structures, Steel and Timber Structures and Applied Mechanics, Building Performance, Urban Physics, Sustainable Retrofit, Regenerative Building Design, structural and architectural design projects, urban-mobility projects and the final disciplinary project. The aggregate 130-EC core component preserves the complete degree without pretending that four mutually exclusive tracks are simultaneously compulsory.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. ENSDELT111 Building with Nature supplies one nature-based engineering and design course; ENSSUST315 Spatial Planning and ENSENVI211 Earth Observation provide spatial planning, GIS, remote sensing and geospatial analysis; ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy, ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design provide environmental-performance and systems perspectives; ENSENVI112 Natural Hazards, ENSENVI212 Soils & Aquifers and ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry add environmental context; BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design provides a product-development project; MCCHEAM111, MCCHEAM212 and MCCHEAM315 address art, architectural history, heritage and material culture; and UCR mathematics, data and research-methods courses supply transferable analysis. These are valuable adjacent offerings, but the workbook contains no architectural or urban-design studio sequence, architectural drawing and physical modelmaking, building structures and applied mechanics sequence, concrete/steel/timber design, building physics, lighting/acoustics and services engineering, construction technology, façade and roof materialisation, real-estate and urban-development project sequence, multidisciplinary building-design project, or 10-EC built-environment Bachelor End Project. Even using every adjacent course would not produce 23 non-PPD courses with concrete relevance to the target's progressive design-and-engineering formation.
